   MINUTES OF MONDAY, MAY 9, 2022
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  LAS ADVISORY COMMITTEE SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Lubisich called the special meeting of the LAS Advisory Committee to order at 5:14 p.m.
on Monday, May 9, 2022 in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Mojarro.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Michelle Brenhaug, Beatriz Mojarro, Chasity Jennings-Nuñez and
  Senya Lubisich.

Commissioners Absent:  None.

ANNOUNCMENTS
Director Perez announced that Councilmember Menchaca will no longer be attending LAS
Advisory Committee meetings, effective today.

Supervisor Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit comments, and
how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR Commission, e-mail all public
comments to mmoralesstevens@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Chair Lubisich hearing no objections, the Agenda Order was approved.

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

LAS ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  MAY 9, 2022
   3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  A. ACTION ITEMS
  A motion was made by Commissioner Brenhaug and seconded by Commissioner
  Mojarro to approve the minutes for January 11, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Jennings-Nuñez. Lubisich, Mojarro,
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. REVIEW OF THE LAS PURPOSE STATEMENT

  Supervisor Morales-Stevens presented the item.

  The Commission asked if the LAS Purpose Statement was posted on-line.

  Public Comment: None

  B. RECAP OF ACTION STEPS TAKEN

  Supervisor Morales-Stevens provided the report.

  The Commission has met with Chief Salas and Chief Morales about the Land
  Acknowledgment Statement.

  The Commission indicated they wanted to identify their stakeholders and discuss
  utilization plan and outreach during this meeting.

  Public Comment: None

  C. DISCUSSION OF MEETINGS WITH CHIEF SALAS AND CHIEF MORALES

  Supervisor Morales-Stevens presented the item.

  The Commission provided information from their meetings with Chief Salas and
  Chief Morales. They discussed prominent places and events where they would like
  the Land Acknowledgment Statement displayed. They shared that Chief Morales is
  motivated to move the process along and the Commission would like to be mindful
  of his time. The Commission stated Chief Salas is requesting that the land be

LAS ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  MAY 9, 2022
   recognized in the statement. They agreed that names of groups and places will
  require clarification.

  D. DISCUSSION OF THE ACTION PLAN

  Supervisor Morales-Stevens presented the item.

  The Commission would like to add the following items to the action plan:

  •  The statement will need to be shared with both tribal leaders to get
  feedback and approval.
  •  They will notify interested groups such as San Gabriel Historical Association,
  Ramona Parlor, Native Suns, San Gabriel Unified School District and the San
  Gabriel Mission Church, when the item will be presented at a meeting to
  give them ample time to review and provide comments.
  •  Under “Create an Outreach Education Plan”, they will include their plan to
  act beyond the statement.

  A motion was made by Vice-Chair Jennings-Nuñez and seconded by Commissioner
  Brenhaug to approve the amended action plan.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Jennings-Nuñez. Lubisich, Mojarro,
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  The Commission began drafting the Land Acknowledgement Statement. After
  discussion, the statement stands as:

  “The City recognizes the unseated villages of the area surrounding the Mission
  leading to the collectivization of the Native peoples”.

  The Commission will review and revise the statement at the following meeting.
  Staff will reach out to Chair Lubisich, Chief Salas and Chief Morales for clarification,
  as needed.

  5. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Lubisich adjourned the meeting at 6:17 p.m.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  August 11, 2022

TO:  Land Acknowledgement Statement Advisory Committee

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  LAS Advisory Committee Approved Action Plan Updated

SUMMARY
The San Gabriel City Council approved the development of the formation of a Land
Acknowledgement Statement (LAS) Advisory Committee to meet with the local tribal groups and
develop a proposed statement.

BACKGROUND
The Historical Preservation and Cultural Resource Commission (HPCRC) discussed the
development of a land acknowledgement statement during their November 4, 2020 commission
meeting. Attachment A includes the research that Community Development staff prepared for the
discussion. This includes general information about how a Land Acknowledgment statement is
used, as well as sample acknowledgment statements.

In line with this, at the June 22, 2021 Human Equity, Access, and Relations (HEAR) Commission
meeting, at the request of Chair Chasity Jennings-Nuñez, staff presented an item on the
development of a land acknowledgment statement for further discussion.

Since both Commissions have expressed interest in creating a statement and since the statement
would ultimately come before City Council for approval, staff presented this item to the Council.

At the August 17, 2021 Council Meeting, City Council approved the creation of an advisory
committee to develop a Land Acknowledgement Statement for the City. This committee is now
known as the Land Acknowledgement Statement Advisory Committee and consists of two
members from City Council, 2 members from the HPCRC and 2 from the HEAR Commission.

At the September 14, 2021 LAS Advisory Committee meeting the members approved the action
plan with amendments.

APPROVED ACTION PLAN
First Meeting

  o Attachment A includes the research provided by the staff to the HPCRC.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  August 11, 2022

TO:  LAS Advisory Committee

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  LAND ACKOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT AND USES

BACKGROUND

At the September 14, 2021 LAS Advisory Committee Meeting, the Committee requested
that staff develop a Purpose Statement and a list of questions for the tribal leaders based
on the Committee’s discussion. At the October 6 meeting the purpose statement and
questions were approved with amendments. The approved statement is as follows: The
Land Acknowledgement Statement serves as a clear and ongoing commitment from the
City of San Gabriel to respect and acknowledge the native peoples of San Gabriel for their
past, current and future contributions to the region. At the May 9, 2022 meeting the
committee provided verbiage for the statement and directed staff to return to the next
meeting with a draft statement.

PROPOSED LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT (LAS)

The City of San Gabriel respectfully acknowledges and recognizes the responsibly to the
original and current care takers of this land (Sibangna). The City recognizes the unseated
villages of the area surrounding the Mission leading to the collectivization of the
indigenous peoples.

POSSIBLE USES FOR THE LAS STATEMENT

The Committee has expressed interest and a need for the City’s land acknowledgement
statement to make a larger impact than simply a statement. Below is what was developed
at the May 9 meeting.
  • Post on the City Website
  • Read aloud at City meetings and functions
  • Post at the front of the Mission Playhouse and/ or City Hall
  • Map of the indigenous villages with the statement
   Land Acknowledgement Statement and Uses
  August 11, 2022
  Page 2

STAFF RECCOMENDATION

Staff recommend that the committee review and approve with or without amendments
the proposed land acknowledgement statement and proposed uses. Upon the
committee’s approval the staff will present the recommendations to the Human Equity,
Access, and Relations (HEAR) and Historical Preservation and Cultural Resource
Commissions for approval. If the two commissions approve the statement it will be
presented to City Council.
